positions.title: Senior Robotics Engineer
positions.description:
Making robots work.  Some tasks:

Robot Kinematics and Dynamics:  implemented in C++; calculates kinematics and dynamics (including Coriolis forces); allows arbitrary joint models; number and types of joints may be specified at run-time; fast:  full dynamics for 8-DOF robot in 15 us on laptop i7; produced Python bindings using SWIG; based on manipulator Jacobian and exponentiation of twists per Murray, Li, Sastry 1994.

Continuum Joint Model:  created novel joint model for constant curvature joint; parametrization is non-singular (unlike current continuum joint models), calculated symbolic rigid body transform, Jacobian, and Jacobian derivatives, using SymPy; needed for kinematics and dynamics of our novel 2-DOF pneumatic actuators; manuscript in preparation.

Robot Modelling:  modeled pressure, position and joint torque for novel 2-DOF pneumatic actuators; modeled inertia of each link, calculated joint torques based on gravity loads; automatically fit models using linear least squares; these models allowed gravity compensation of robot arm, substantially improving performance.

Robot GUI:  developed GUI in Python to visualize robot and control robot joint angles directly or in Euclidean space through inverse kinematics; based on Qt, OpenGL, and proprietary Otherlab code; integrated with ROS to receive robot state information and send robot joint commands; fiducial detection projects rendered robots into video frames, i.e. augmented reality.

Fiducial Based Robot State Estimation:  integrated machine vision cameras and fiducial detection algorithm (ChiliTags) to estimate robot state; camera position estimated based on tags on robot base, avoiding camera position calibration; position of robot gripper estimated using OpenCV solvePnP; calibrated cameras using OpenCV tools; benchmarked fiducial detection algorithms and machine vision cameras; produced Python bindings for ChiliTags using SWIG.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
PhD Candidate working for Joel Burdick researching robotic grasping.

Caging:  academic research in caging - a form of grasping where the object is not immobilized but is prevented from escaping from the hand; created and implemented simple algorithms to calculate cages for polygons and 3D polytopes with two point fingers using contact-space (where both fingers touch the object); described topological relationship between contact space the objects configuration space; generated catalog of and characterization method for all types of 2D and 3D grasps of polytopes; created and implemented the first algorithm to calculate exact cages for convex polygons with three fingers that are robust to finger position perturbation; see publications.

Robot Kinematics:  solved closed form kinematics for 7-DOF Barrett WAM arm; implemented in C; samples over shoulder yaw angle and finds 8 possible solutions; correct identification of which leaf a solution belongs to aids in finding continuous inverse kinematic paths; found geometric insight that avoids sampling over angles that have no solutions; implemented inverse kinematics for general six-revolute-joint manipulator; based on Manocha and Canny, and Raghavan and Roth; uses polynomial ideals to convert IK problem into finding the eigenvalues of a 24x24 matrix; implemented local inverse kinematics using local Jacobian methods including damped and selectively damped least squares methods.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Graduate student researcher at JPL during my stay at Caltech.

DARPA ARM Program:  Part of the Caltech-JPL team in the DARPA Autonomous Robotic Manipulation - Software (ARM-S) competition to advance the state of the art of robotic manipulation.  The team took first place.  Responsible for robot motion planning, grasp planning, and manipulation planning.

RCTA:   Part of JPL’s team in the Army Research Lab's Robotics Collaborative Technology Alliance to develop autonomous capabilities and robot/human interfaces for a Dragon Runner DR20 mobility platform equipped with a 4-DOF arm and gripper.  Responsible for grasping.

Robot Motion Planning:  created GUI to visualize and test robot arm for DARPA’s Autonomous Robotic Manipulation program; robot was two 7-DOF Barrett WAM arms; created tools to save and modify robot and world states to test planning on previously detected or modified scenes; identified key bug in planning software; produced tools to move robot arms at joint level or in Euclidean space; wrote nearly all code (except for RRT-connect algorithm) for planning in C, GUI in C++.

Grasp Planning:  wrote online grasp planner to produce hand pose relative to object as well as finger angles; algorithm picked semi-random hand positions and simulated moving towards object and closing fingers (collisions modelled using JPL’s DARTS tools); created metrics to rank grasp quality; worked on primitives fit to point clouds or known object models; created GUI to visualize grasps and tools to save and modify sets of grasps; this tool created all grasps used by JPL in DARPA ARM Phase II program.

positions.title: Mechanical Engineer
positions.description: Mechanical design for space mechanisms.  Produced design and CAD models of parts (uisng IDEAS, but also proficient in SolidWorks).  Produced drawings and worked with machine shops to produce these parts.  Designed test fixtures.  Validated flight hardware.  Designed novel  counterweighted mobile-like test equipment to deploy a five panel solar array from a 1-DOF rail.  Proficient in geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T).  Familiar with military specifications.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Designed and fabricated mechanical components of precision 2D optical slope sensor; studied Japanese language, writing, and culture.
